title: Quick Molten Uruguayan Beef Empanadas
description: Buttery and molten empanadas filled with Uruguayan beef and rum, shaped like nigiri for a unique twist, perfect for a flexitarian snack
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large skillet, cook the ground beef over medium high heat until browned, breaking it up into small pieces as it cooks.
Add the chopped onion to the skillet and cook until it is translucent.
Stir in the rum, salt, and pepper, and cook for 1 minute.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out the empanada dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Use a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass to cut out circles of dough.
Place a tablespoon of the beef mixture in the center of each dough circle.
Brush the edges of the dough with the melted butter, then fold the dough in half over the filling to form a half moon shape, pressing the edges together to seal.
Use your fingers to shape the empanadas into nigiri shapes.
Place the empanadas on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving about 1 inch of space between each empanada.
Brush the tops of the empanadas with the beaten eggs.
Bake the empanadas in the preheated oven for 15 minutes, or until golden brown.
Cook ground beef to an internal temperature of 71°C / 160°F (no longer pink in the middle) before serving.
